walkthroughs.h2: Henry II and the rise of common law
walkthroughs.body_html: Henry II (1154-89) standardised royal justice through itinerant judges, jury trial and the General Eyre. The Assize of Clarendon (1166) established procedures for criminal accusation. Royal writs displaced lordly courts, embedding a common law applied throughout the kingdom and laying foundations for later constitutional development.

walkthroughs.h2: Why did the barons revolt in 1215?
walkthroughs.body_html: King John lost Normandy in 1204, levied repeated scutage to fund failed reconquest, and quarrelled with Pope Innocent III. Defeat at Bouvines in 1214 destroyed his credibility. Northern barons rebelled, occupied London in May 1215 and forced John to seal Magna Carta on 15 June, restraining arbitrary taxation and imprisonment.

Innocent III annulled Magna Carta within months, but it was reissued in 1216, 1217 and definitively in 1225. Clause 39 inspired later appeals to due process, including the seventeenth-century parliamentarians and the American constitutional tradition. Its enduring power lay less in 1215 specifics than in symbolising lawful limits on monarchy.

mcqs.q: What did Magna Carta actually do in 1215?
options: It was a peace treaty between King John and rebel barons protecting baronial privileges and limiting arbitrary royal taxation and imprisonment — it was annulled within months.
Magna Carta gave ordinary English people democratic rights and freedom.
Crusaders went to find the Holy Grail.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.

mcqs.q: Why is Magna Carta still cited in 'Power and the People' history?
options: Magna Carta directly created modern human rights in 1215.
Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
Magna Carta gave the right to vote to all English men.
Because clauses on lawful judgement and protection from arbitrary imprisonment were reinterpreted in the 17th century to support broader liberties, even though they originally protected only barons.

mcqs.q: Why did the First Crusade happen?

A mix of Byzantine appeals for help, papal ambition to reunite Christendom under Rome, religious enthusiasm, land hunger among younger sons, and indulgences offered to fighters.
Christians launched the Crusades to convert Muslims to Christianity.
